newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hongkong Bank FRCD raised to HK$2.5 bln.
newsitem.headline: Hongkong Bank FRCD raised to HK$2.5 bln.

text.p: Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corp's floating rate certificates of deposit issue due May 2000 has been increased to HK$2.5 billion from HK$2.0 billion, said bookrunner HSBC Markets.
The issue was off the bank's HK$20 billion CD programme.
The three-year certificates were launched on April 23 and priced at par to float at 22 basis points over the one-month Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate.
With fees, the all-in return for top-tier managers is 27 basis points.
Application has been made to the Hong Kong Monetary Authority to accept the issue as eligible for its Liquidity Adjustment Facility, or discount window.
Arranger and bookrunner HSBC Markets committed to HK$500 million.

Co-lead managers, with HK$140 million each, are Banque Nationale de Paris's Hongkong branch, China Development Finance Co (Hong Kong), Commerz (East Asia), DKB Asia, Fuji International Finance (HK), Hang Seng Bank, Jardine Fleming Bank, Paribas Asia, Tokyo-Mitsubishi International (HK), Union Bank of Switzerland's Hongkong branch, Westdeutsche Landesbank's Hongkong branch and Westpac Banking Corp's Hongkong branch.
Senior managers, with HK$90 million each, are Amoy Treasury Ltd, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and SGZ-Bank.
Manager Chase Manhattan Asia committed to HK$50 million.
The signing is tentatively set for May 16 and the payment date for May 23.
